issue: PMAT-629 (closes forjar#629) — nightly.yml rebuilt only when a commit landed in the last 24 hours, so a commit followed by a quiet day, or a failed nightly, was never built; the nightly sat 12 days behind main. The gate now builds whenever refs/tags/nightly is absent or is not HEAD, and the release pins the tag to the built commit.

falsification.test: a_nightly_behind_head_on_a_quiet_day_is_rebuilt, a_nightly_at_head_is_not_rebuilt, a_repo_with_no_nightly_tag_builds, the_nightly_tag_is_pinned_to_the_built_commit — all written by this branch. The first three EXECUTE the workflow gate script lifted from the parsed YAML against synthetic repositories whose commits are 30 days old.
falsification.observed_failure: Declared mutations against the workflow, each restored byte-identical after: restore the 24h gate -> 2 failed (behind-HEAD quiet day, no tag); make the gate unconditional -> 1 failed (tag at HEAD); delete target_commitish -> 1 failed (tag pin). Restored: 4 passed.

systems: Nix Hydra: a job is built when its derivation output is not already in the store — keyed on inputs, never on how recently something changed [X]; this gate keys on the commit the published artifact names
Bazel: an action reruns when its action-key digest misses the cache, so a failed or skipped build is retried on the next invocation by construction — the property the 24h gate lacked
Launchpad daily recipe builds: a daily build is dispatched only when the recipe branch revision differs from the last built one, the same published-vs-source comparison as tag-vs-HEAD
crux.verdict: No crux row is owed: CI configuration only, no shipped behaviour and no CHANGELOG bullet. Every surveyed system decides by comparing what is published to the source, not by wall-clock activity, which is the change made here.
